title: Stephen Curry
wiki_lead:
Wardell Stephen Curry II ( STEF-ən; born March 14, 1988), also known as Steph Curry ( STEF), is an American professional basketball player for the Golden State Warriors of the National Basketball Association (NBA), where he plays as a point guard. Nicknamed "Chef Curry", he is widely regarded as the greatest shooter in basketball history and one of the greatest players of all time. He is credited with revolutionizing the game by popularizing the three-point shot across all levels of basketball.
Curry is a four-time NBA champion, a two-time NBA Most Valuable Player (MVP), an NBA Finals MVP, and a two-time NBA All-Star Game MVP. He is also a two-time NBA scoring champion, a 12-time NBA All-Star, and an 11-time All-NBA Team selection (including four on the First Team). Internationally, he has won two gold medals at the FIBA World Cup and a gold medal at the 2024 Summer Olympics as part of the U.S. national team.
Curry played collegiately for the Davidson Wildcats, where he was named Conference Player of the Year twice. He set the NCAA single-season record for three-pointers made (162) as a sophomore and led the NCAA Division I in scoring during his junior year. Curry was selected by the Warriors as the seventh overall pick in the 2009 NBA draft.
In 2014–15, Curry won his first league MVP award and led the Warriors to their first championship since 1975. The following season, he became the first player to be unanimously voted MVP and to lead the league in scoring while shooting above 50–40–90. That same year, the Warriors broke the record for most wins in a regular season (73) en route to the 2016 NBA Finals, where they lost a 3–1 series lead to the Cleveland Cavaliers. Curry then helped the Warriors win back-to-back titles in 2017 and 2018, and reach the 2019 NBA Finals, where they fell to the Toronto Raptors in six games. In 2021, Curry led the league in scoring for a second time in his career. The following season, Curry won his fourth championship and first Finals MVP award, leading the Warriors past the Boston Celtics in six games in the 2022 NBA Finals. That same season, he became the NBA's all-time leader in three-pointers made, surpassing Ray Allen.
Curry has the highest career free-throw percentage in NBA history (.912) and has led the league in three-pointers made a record eight times. In 2016, he broke his own record for three-pointers made in a regular season, with 402, and made at least one three-pointer in an NBA-record 268 consecutive games from 2018 to 2023.
Curry was named one of Time's 100 most influential people in the world in 2016 and has been listed by Forbes as one of the world's ten highest-paid athletes nine times. He has also been listed as the highest paid NBA player for a record nine consecutive seasons and has led the NBA in worldwide jersey sales six times.

grok_lead: Wardell Stephen Curry II (born March 14, 1988), commonly known as Steph Curry, is an American professional basketball player who stands 6 ft 2 in (1.88 m) and serves as the point guard for the Golden State Warriors of the National Basketball Association (NBA). Drafted seventh overall by the Warriors in the 2009 NBA draft out of Davidson College, Curry has spent his entire professional career with the franchise, emerging as one of the league's transformative figures through his unprecedented long-range shooting accuracy and volume. Curry's career highlights include four NBA championships in 2015, 2017, 2018, and 2022, two regular-season Most Valuable Player awards in 2015 and 2016 (the latter being the first unanimous selection in NBA history), and the Finals MVP award in 2022. He has been selected to 11 All-Star games, earned 11 All-NBA honors, and holds the NBA record for career three-point field goals made, surpassing 4,000 with a career average exceeding 24 points per game across over 1,000 regular-season appearances. Internationally, Curry contributed to the United States ' gold medal at the 2024 Summer Olympics, where he led scoring efforts in key victories. Curry's playing style, characterized by off-ball movement, quick release, and elite ball-handling, has empirically shifted NBA strategies toward greater emphasis on three-point shooting, with league-wide attempts rising sharply during his prime years due to the causal influence of his efficiency and success. Despite early career challenges with ankle injuries that tested his durability, his sustained performance into his late 30s underscores a combination of skill, conditioning, and tactical adaptation.
